questions.q: How do you create a PivotChart from an existing PivotTable?
options: Select a cell inside the PivotTable and choose Insert Chart from the ribbon
Manually redraw the PivotTable's data as a new, separate chart
PivotCharts cannot be created from an existing PivotTable — they require a fresh raw range
Copy the PivotTable's values and paste them into a chart template
questions.explain: With a cell inside the PivotTable selected, Insert Chart builds a PivotChart directly from that PivotTable's current rows, columns, and values.

questions.q: What is the critical difference between a PivotChart and a normal Excel chart built from a static range?
options: A PivotChart stays linked to its PivotTable and updates automatically when the PivotTable's structure changes
A PivotChart can only display data as a pie chart
A normal chart automatically updates when its source range changes, but a PivotChart never does
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: Rearranging a PivotTable's fields — swapping Rows for Columns, adding a Filter, changing the aggregation — automatically updates the linked PivotChart, with no rebuilding needed.

questions.q: What are field buttons, and why are they unique to PivotCharts?
options: Interactive dropdown controls Excel places directly on a PivotChart for its Rows/Columns/Filters — a standard chart has no live connection to a PivotTable's fields to expose such controls for
Buttons that convert a PivotChart back into a plain range
A feature available on every Excel chart, not just PivotCharts
Buttons used only to change a chart's color scheme
questions.explain: Field buttons let you filter or rearrange a PivotChart directly from the chart itself. A standard chart has no equivalent because it has no live connection to a PivotTable's field structure.

questions.q: Do slicers and Timelines (from Lesson 15) work on PivotCharts?
options: Yes — a slicer or Timeline connected to the underlying PivotTable also filters any PivotChart built from it
No — slicers and Timelines only ever affect PivotTables, never PivotCharts
Only Timelines work on PivotCharts; slicers do not
Only if the PivotChart is rebuilt after the slicer is added
questions.explain: Since a PivotChart is a visual reflection of its PivotTable, any slicer or Timeline connected to that PivotTable also filters the chart — exactly how a dashboard sheet updates everything from one click.

questions.q: In a dashboard-style workbook, what happens when a connected Timeline is dragged to a new date range?
options: The PivotTable and every PivotChart built from it update simultaneously, all from that one action
Only the PivotTable updates; each PivotChart must be manually refreshed afterward
The Timeline only affects the worksheet it's physically placed on, regardless of connections
Dragging a Timeline has no effect on any linked PivotChart
questions.explain: A single Timeline drag updates the PivotTable and every connected PivotChart at once — the core mechanic that makes a dashboard-style workbook feel interactive rather than static.
